title: Integral base replacement preserves the module base-change isomorphism
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $p':X'\to S'$, $\pi:S''\to S'$,
$p'':X''\to S''$, $\pi':X''\to X'$, $g':T\to S''$, $e:Y\to T$ and
$h'':Y\to X''$ be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $\pi$ is integral
[def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and that $(\pi',p'',p',\pi)$ and
$(e,h'',g',p'')$ are Cartesian squares [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].
Let the pasted square have edges $(e,\pi'\circ h'',\pi\circ g',p')$.
For every integer $q$ and every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site
of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the canonical degree-$q$ base-change map of the
pasted square [sbc-def-base-change-map] is an isomorphism if and only if the canonical
map of the square over $S''$ is an isomorphism. No surjectivity or lower-degree
base-change hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0F05, lemma-base-change-q-integral-bottom, proof; the converse follows from its two displayed pushforward identifications. Exact arbitrary-ring formulation: WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/SmoothBaseChange/IntegralBaseChange.lean, isIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_iff_of_isIntegralHom, lines 229-239.

proof.text: Integral morphisms are stable under base change, so pi-prime is integral. Integral direct image is exact; the same assertion for module sheaves follows by the exact, faithful coefficient forgetful functor. Exact inverse images and exact integral pushforwards compute their own bounded-below derived functors.

The canonical integral underived exchange is invertible. Extend it termwise and use exactness to obtain the canonical derived exchange for the integral square. Insert the derived direct-image composition comparisons into the vertical pasting identity. On F in degree zero, apply degree-q homology and the exact-functor homology comparisons. This identifies the pasted degreewise arrow with integral pushforward of the inner degreewise arrow, conjugated by endpoint isomorphisms. These are the comparisons implemented by nonempty_arrowIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_comp in the source module.

If the inner arrow is invertible, its pushforward and its conjugate pasted arrow are invertible. Conversely integral pushforward detects zero module sheaves. Its exactness identifies the pushforwards of the kernel and cokernel with the kernel and cokernel of the pushed arrow. If the latter is invertible both vanish, so detection makes the original arrow mono and epi, hence invertible. This proves both implications, including empty schemes and negative degrees.

lean.statement:
theorem Etale.isIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_iff_of_isIntegralHom (π : S'' ⟶ S') [IsIntegralHom π]
    (hπ : IsPullback π' p'' p' π) (sq'' : IsPullback e h'' g' p'')
    (sq : IsPullback e (h'' ≫ π') (g' ≫ π) p') (q : ℤ)
    (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) :
    IsIso (Etale.baseChangeHomologyMap Λ sq q F) ↔
      IsIso (Etale.baseChangeHomologyMap Λ sq'' q F)
